name: Johan August Blom

identity.occupation: Editor and part-owner of the liberal newspaper Fyrisposten
identity.home: The newspaper office and flat above it on Drottninggatan, Uppsala, smelling of ink and wet paper
identity.appearance: Heavy-set and red-cheeked, with a magnificent brown beard, a cigar he rarely lights, and shirt cuffs grey with printer's ink.

drives.text: Keep the paper's subscribers ahead of the conservative rival across the river.
Push the cause of reform: schools, railways, an end to superstition and to the clergy's grip on the countryside.
Get the true story of what the Society does, whatever it is, and print it first.

voice.register: Booming, jovial and argumentative; speaks in headlines and leading articles even across a dinner table.
mannerisms: Taps the table with a folded newspaper to make a point
Calls everyone 'my friend' especially when he disagrees
Repeats a good phrase twice to remember it for print
sampleLines: My friend, the age of trolls is over. The age of the telegraph is here. Superstition in the countryside, that's the headline, that's the story.
You've been to Hedesunda twice this month. I don't ask why. I merely note it. I am a noting sort of man.
Give me something true and I'll print it straight. Give me nothing and I shall have to print what people say, and people say such things.

background: Blom was a schoolteacher in Västerås until a sharp article on the cathedral chapter cost him his post. He drifted into journalism in Stockholm, came to Uppsala to run Fyrisposten in 1864, and has turned a dull advertiser into a lively, quarrelsome liberal paper read in every coffee house in town. He mocks rural superstition in print as a matter of policy, but he is too good a newspaperman not to notice that certain country stories keep ending with the arrival of the same gentlefolk from Gamla Uppsala. He does not yet know whether the Society are a story about fraud, about science, or about something else.

latentHooks.text: He pays small sums to servants, coachmen and telegraph clerks for news, and some of them work close to the Society.
A libel suit from a Uppsala alderman is pending, and losing it would ruin him; he would trade a great deal for leverage.
His younger sister has been in the asylum at Uppsala for ten years after seeing 'the woman in the lake'; he visits her monthly and tells no one.
He means to stand for the second chamber of the Riksdag, and a sensational exposé would make his name across the county.

networkLinks.nature: Editor with correspondents in the provincial papers
networkLinks.influence: Can put a story in print across the county within the week, praising or mocking the Society.

networkLinks.nature: Drinks with junior constables who sell him the night's arrests
networkLinks.influence: Can learn of the Society's dealings with the police almost as soon as they happen.

networkLinks.nature: Buys road gossip from Brita Strand
networkLinks.influence: Learns who has been coming and going from the Society's headquarters.

attitudeReason: Neither friend nor foe; the Society is a story he has not yet decided how to write.
